Source disagreements are recorded in source_conflicts, not silently resolved.
STEP 1 grades were not defended; each case was re-graded from the verification evidence alone, including downgrades to B or C where warranted.
STEP 1 and STEP 2 files were not modified.

cases.project_name: General Motors North American assembly plants (Fort Wayne IN, Silao Mexico, Wentzville MO) — April 2021 shutdown wave
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED. Fort Wayne and Silao paused 1 week; Wentzville paused 2 weeks, per GM's April 8, 2021 announcement. GM's own statement: 'These recent scheduling adjustments are being driven by the continued parts shortages caused by semiconductor supply constraints from international markets experiencing COVID-19-related restrictions.'
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED. Vehicle assembly line operation (not a construction milestone); specific product lines named — Silverado/Sierra HD trucks at Fort Wayne, midsize trucks and full-size vans at Wentzville.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED, directly from GM's own dated announcement, cross-confirmed via Washington Post, CNBC, and WANE 15 (Fort Wayne local coverage).
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED (general). GM prioritized available semiconductor supply toward its most profitable/high-demand vehicles; no finer-grained mitigation detail was found.
cases.response_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the general strategy; no finer detail found.
cases.source_conflicts: No conflict on the April 2021 figures themselves, but important newly-found context: this was NOT an isolated event. The same GM plants experienced repeat chip-shortage shutdowns later in 2021 too — another wave in July 2021 (Flint, Silao, Fort Wayne, week of 7/26-8/2) and again in September 2021 (Fort Wayne/Silao week of 9/6; Wentzville weeks of 9/6 AND 9/13). This candidate is scoped specifically to the April 8, 2021 wave, as in STEP 1, but the broader pattern was a chronic, recurring disruption through 2021 rather than a single one-time event.

cases.project_name: Ford Kansas City Assembly Plant (Claycomo, Missouri) — F-150 / Transit production
cases.event_date: 2021-05-17 (first shutdown of this pair); second shutdown began 2021-07-12
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED. Plant halted F-150 and Transit van production for two weeks starting May 17, 2021; halted again starting July 12, 2021 (F-150 line, 2 weeks) and July 19, 2021 (Transit vans, 1 week). Ford's official statement: 'The global semiconductor shortage continues to affect global automakers and other industries in all parts of the world,' and that Ford was 'prioritizing completing our customers' vehicles that were assembled without certain parts.'
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED. Specific product lines (F-150 pickup line, Transit cargo van line) within the same plant, with independently-tracked shutdown durations.
cases.delay_value: 2 (weeks, May shutdown); 2 (weeks, July F-150); 1 (week, July Transit)
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED, corroborated across WHAS11, Fox4KC, and CBS News.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED (general). Ford prioritized completing partially-assembled vehicles awaiting missing chip-dependent parts rather than halting all output; no more specific chip-allocation strategy for this plant was found.
cases.response_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the general statement; INFERRED/not found for finer detail.
cases.source_conflicts: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO STEP 1: STEP 1's candidate L3-017 incorrectly bundled a January 2021 'Ford Focus plant' full-month shutdown together with this Kansas City case, both labeled country 'USA.' Verification found the Focus-plant shutdown actually occurred at Ford's Saarlouis, GERMANY plant (Ford's sole European Focus manufacturing site) — Focus was discontinued in North America years earlier, so a US 'Focus plant' cannot exist. That event has been split out as a separate, corrected case (V3-004) with the correct country. The Kansas City figures documented here are independently confirmed and do not depend on the corrected Focus/Saarlouis facts.

cases.project_name: VinFast Manufacturing US LLC plant, Chatham County 'Moncure megasite'
cases.risk_category: regulation/permitting, compounded with contractual default / financial (capital-allocation) factors
cases.event_date: 2022-03 (original deal announced); key subsequent dates: 2024-05-10 (first extension request), 2024-12 (site work stops after 2023 tree-clearing), 2026-01-06 (NC AG default notice), 2026-03 (scaled-back permit proposal, ~1,400 jobs), 2026-05-21 (state sues to reclaim the site), 2026-07-27 (Chatham County terminates its economic development agreement with VinFast)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, and substantially more severe than STEP 1 captured. This is no longer simply a delayed project: as of the most recent reporting reviewed (2026-07-27), Chatham County has formally terminated its incentive agreement and the State of North Carolina is suing to reclaim the site, because VinFast never resumed substantive construction after clearing trees in 2023. The original 2022 deal promised 7,500 jobs and a 2024 production start; VinFast's last proposal (March 2026) had shrunk to roughly 1,400 jobs and possibly just a distribution center rather than a full car factory.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED, precise. Site was cleared of trees in 2023 (an early WBS-equivalent stage) but no further construction occurred after December 2024 — the project stalled between 'site clearing' and 'vertical construction' and never resumed.
cases.delay_value: not applicable as a single figure — the project's status changed from 'delayed' to 'terminated/defaulted,' a different outcome category than a completed-but-late project. From the original 2024 production target to the July 2026 contract termination is roughly 26+ months if a raw count is wanted, but this conflates delay with outright failure.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the sequence of dated milestones; each date is corroborated across multiple outlets (Spectrum Local News, WUNC, Axios Raleigh, Chapelboro, WRAL, NC Newsline).
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. VinFast repeatedly requested schedule extensions (first 2024-05-10, citing a global EV sales slowdown affecting its financing) and ultimately proposed a drastically scaled-back project (from 7,500 to approximately 1,400 jobs) rather than completing the original plan.
cases.source_conflicts: WRAL reports a factual dispute at the center of the lawsuit itself: VinFast executives claim they were about to resume 'vertical' construction as recently as March 2026, while the state's lawsuit disputes whether any genuine construction activity ever occurred; the two sides disagree on the very definition of 'vertical construction activity,' which is a live, unresolved legal dispute, not merely a reporting discrepancy.

Additionally, 'production equipment installation completed by spring 2026' is a different milestone (equipment readiness) from 'mass production start' (output), and some sources may conflate the two; this candidate treats trial-production start (2026-09-22, well multi-source confirmed) as the only firmly OBSERVED date.

cases.project_name: Intel Ohio One (New Albany, Ohio) semiconductor fabs
cases.risk_category: regulation/policy & funding uncertainty (no clean fit in the 8-category taxonomy)
cases.event_date: 2025-02-28 (most recent major restatement; now confirmed via Intel's own official newsroom page, not just press coverage)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, now confirmed via a PRIMARY company source (Intel Newsroom, 'Ohio One Construction Timeline Update'): Mod 1 construction completion now targeted for 2030, operations beginning 2030-2031; Mod 2 construction completion 2031, operations beginning 2032. Chip production was originally slated to begin in 2025 when the $28B investment was announced in 2022 — a slip of roughly 5-6 years from the original public target to the current one.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED, moderately precise: Intel's own newsroom describes concrete milestones reached (6.4 million work-hours to date, 200,000+ cubic yards of concrete poured, sub-utility trenches complete, a 'go vertical' milestone achieved with the below-grade structure complete and above-ground structure now underway) — i.e., site/foundation work is well along even though the overall completion date has slipped repeatedly.
cases.delay_value: approx. 5 (original 2025 target -> current ~2030 Mod 1 operations target)
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED for each individual restatement (2022 target, a 2024 delay, the Feb 2025 delay to 2030), each separately and officially dated — but this is a compounding SEQUENCE of at least 3 separate delay announcements over 3 years, not one clean single-event delay.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Construction continues (not halted) at a deliberately slower pace; Intel's own statement attributed this to 'taking a prudent approach to ensure we complete the project in a financially responsible manner' (EVP Naga Chandrasekaran). Per Intel's own newsroom page, physical construction work is actively continuing rather than being paused entirely.
cases.primary_source: Intel Newsroom, 'Ohio One Construction Timeline Update,' https://newsroom.intel.com/corporate/ohio-one-construction-timeline-update ; CNBC, 2025-02-28, https://www.cnbc.com/2025/02/28/intel-delays-ohio-plant-opening-to-2030-production-was-to-start-2026.html
cases.source_conflicts: The cumulative delay figure depends on which original baseline is used: '2025' (the target stated when the $28B investment was announced in 2022) versus an intermediate '2026' target that some 2024-era reporting cites (suggesting the public target itself moved at least once before the widely-reported Feb 2025 restatement to 2030). This candidate treats the earliest publicly announced 2025 target (2022 announcement) as the baseline, consistent with STEP 1, but notes that at least one intermediate target (2026) also existed at some point, not independently pinned to an exact announcement date in this pass.

cases.project_name: Ford BlueOval City / 'Tennessee Truck Plant' (formerly 'Tennessee Electric Vehicle Center')
cases.risk_category: none of the eight listed categories fit; originally demand/strategy-driven, and now additionally a full product-scope change
cases.event_date: 2025-12-15/16 (Ford scraps the electric pickup program entirely)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, and substantially more severe than STEP 1 captured. STEP 1 recorded only the 2024-08-22 delay from 2025 to 2027. Verification found a much larger subsequent change: in December 2025, Ford scrapped the electric pickup truck planned for BlueOval City entirely and pivoted to gas-powered 'Built Ford Tough' truck models, renaming the facility from 'Tennessee Electric Vehicle Center' to 'Tennessee Truck Plant.' The new target for gas-truck production start is 2029 (not 2027). As of mid-2026, the plant has not yet begun any production.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED at a program level, but NOT usable at fine WBS-task granularity, because the change is a full product-line replacement (electric pickup -> gas-powered truck), not a schedule slip on the same task.
cases.delay_value: not applicable as a single figure — the object being measured (which vehicle program) changed entirely partway through, so a before/after day-count for 'the same task' is not well-defined. A coarse figure (original 2025/2026 target for the EV -> 2029 target for the DIFFERENT gas-truck product) would conflate delay with scope change and is not reported here as a delay figure.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED for each individual dated announcement (Aug 2024: 2025->2027 for the EV; Dec 2025: EV canceled, gas truck targeted for 2029). INFERRED/not meaningful for any single 'total delay' figure given the scope change.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Ford fully canceled the planned electric pickup and redirected the plant to gas-powered truck production, citing 'lower-than-expected demand, high costs and regulatory changes.' Current employment is 80 people, with a target of 2,300 once gas-truck production ramps.
cases.source_conflicts: WREG states 'the original timeline had trucks coming off the assembly line by 2026; last year [2025], that timeline was pushed back to 2027' — this differs slightly from STEP 1's baseline, which described the pre-delay target as '2025' rather than '2026.' Given the subsequent full product-scope change (EV to gas truck), reconciling the exact original numeric target is now moot for ground-truth purposes.
